caseno: Appeal from Original Order No. 84 of 1974.
lawyer:
M. H. Khondker with Abu Backkar and Akram Hossain Amin ----- For Appellant.
Faqeer Abdul Mannan ----- For Respondents.
parties:
Musammat Rabeya Khatun ----- Appellant.
Vs.
Md. Elias Mollah and ors ----- Respondents.
full_judgment:
2. The plaintiff-Respondents have brought the aforesaid suit for a declaration which has been worded in the following manner: 

 "For a decree that the sale deed bearing No. 2721-64 executed on 30.4.71 and registered on 18.6.71 as mentioned in schedule 'A' and A(1) below in respect of the property as mentioned in Schedule 'B' below as also the purported sale deed executed by the defendant Nos. 1-2 in favour of defendant No. 3 relating to the self-same property are void, illegal, inoperative, collusive and the defendants, Nos. 1-2 have acquired no interest in the said property and hence not binding on the plaintiffs." 

 3. According to the allegations made in the plaint, the property described in Schedule B originally belonged to one Jashoda Lal Basu who died leaving behind seven sons as his heirs and Al-Haj Sk. Alam Shah Mollah has acquired the right title and interest of the said property from the said 7 sons of Jashoda Lal on the basis of a registered deed of sale in the benami of his wife Mst. Sudan. Bewa, Defendant No. 5 in the suit The entire consideration money was paid by the husband and after the death of AI-Haj Alam Shah Mollah, the property devolved upon his four sons, Plaintiffs 1-3 and another, four daughters and the widow, Defendant No. 5. After the death of their father, the plaintiffs filed a suit in the 6th Court of Munsif, Dacca being Title Suit No. 220 of 1970 for a declaration that the deed of sale in the name of Surjan Bewa, Defendant No. 5, in respect of Schedule B property was a benami transaction and the plaintiffs were the owners of the said property to the extent of -/8/- annas 6 gondas and odd. The said suit was contested by defendant No. 5 but the suit was decreed in favour of the plain-tiffs on 21.6.72. During the pendency of the suit the plaintiffs obtained an injunction restraining Surjan Bewa, Defendant No. 5. who was Defendant No. 1 of the said suit, from dis-possessing the plaintiffs from the said property. Defendant No. 5, however, after the institution of the said suit left the suit premises and executed and registered a kabala in favour of Defendant No. 1 and 2 in respect of the entire property mentioned in Schedule B on 30-4-71 and the said deed was registered on 18-6-71. It has subsequently transpired that Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 created another deed of sale in respect of the suit premises in favour of Defendant No. 3 on 26-6-73 and it has been alleged in paragraph 14 of the plaint that "as cloud has been cast by creation of the aforesaid sham sale deed on the basis of which Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 are making attempts to dispossess the plaintiffs from the Schedule 'B' property, the plaintiffs have been complied to file the present suit for declaration to the effect that the kabala as mentioned in the schedule 'A" is fraudulent and not binding on the plaintiffs." 

 4. It has been further stated in paragraph 14(a) of the plaint, which was added by an amendment of the plaint, that "on getting scent of the preparation for filing the present suit the defendants Nos. 1 and 2 have created a so-called sale deed dated 26.6.73 in respect of the property mentioned in Schedule 'B' below in favour of the one Mst. Rabeya Khatun, wife of Ali Ahmed of 66/1, Dakshin Maisundi i.e. Defendant No. 3, fraudulently and collusively and without any consideration with the object of creating hindrances and obstacles in the way of peaceful enjoyment and undisturbed possession of the property in suit and thereby another cloud has been created upon the light, title and interest of the plaintiffs and the same is also required to be removed. The so called sale deed dated 26.6.73 created by the Defendant No. 1 and 2 in favour of the Defendant No. 3 is void, illegal, inoperative and no right, title and interest has accrued thereby on pendant No. 3 and inasmuch as the Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 acquired no right, title and interest in the property. Moreover the right, title and interest of the plaintiffs in property described in the Schedule 'B' has been affected by the said collusive and fraudulent sale deed." 

 5. After the filing of the suit, an application dated 6.2.73 for an order of temporary injunction against Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 restraining them from entering into the suit premises mentioned in Schedule B and from disturbing the plaintiffs peaceful possession in the suit property till disposal of this suit was filed, but the said application was rejected, as none appeared to move that application. The plaintiffs filed a petition for amendment of the plaint on 10.7.73 incorporating a statement as paragraph 14(a) in the plaint relating to the subsequent transfer made by Defendant No. 1 and 2 in favour of Defendant No. 3 and thereafter an application was again filed on 14.7.73 for an order of temporary injunction for restraining Defendant No. 3 from entering into the suit premises. Upon the said application, the learned Subordinate Judge by his order dated 21.7.73 directed issue of notice upon Defendant No. 3 to show cause against the prayer made in the petition for temporary injunction and at the same time issued an ad interim order of injunction restraining Defendant No. 3 from .entering into-the premises in suit till the disposal of the same. 

 6. Thereafter Defendant No. 3 appeared in the suit and filed a written objection contending, inter alia, that the plaintiff's prayer for temporary injunction was not maintainable. The substantive defense taken in the application is that .the suit premises was acquired by Mst. Surjan Bibi, Defendant No. 5, in her own interest and she was not the benamder of he husband, AI-Haj Alam Shah Mollah, that Surjan Bewa transferred the suit properties to Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 for Tk. 28,000/- by a registered sale deed dated 30.4.71 and delivered possession of the same to them, that thereafter Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 got their names mutated, paid rent, possessed the suit land for some time and contracted to sell the same property to Defendant No. 3 for a sum of. Tk. 40,000/- of which a sum of Tk. 10,000/- was paid as earnest money and inducted Defendant No. 3 in a portion of the suit premises on 20.10.71, that during the War of Liberation the defendants had to leave the suit premises on 3.12.71 and that when in the middle of March, 1972 Defendant No. 3 went to possess the suit premises found the plaintiffs in possession thereof and thereafter Defendant No. 3 filed a petition before the S.D.O (s) Dacca under the provision of P. O. No.18 of 1972 praying for restoration of possessive in the suit premises and that before the S.D.O. could pass an order of eviction of the plaintiffs from the suit premises the present suit has been filed to forestall any effective action which could be taken under the aforesaid Presidential Order. 

 7. The learned Subordinate Judge has taken a view, on a consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case, that the plaintiffs have got a prima facie case for temporary injunction and that it having been admitted that the plaintiffs ale in possession of the suit premises and defendant No. 3 is out of possession of the same, the balance of conference and inconvenience is also in favour of the plaintiffs. Ad interim order of injunction has been made absolute on the said view of the matter. 

 8. Mr. M. H. Khondker, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of defendant No. 3, who is the sole appellant 111 this appeal, contends that having regard to the nature of the suit which has been instituted by the plaintiff-respondents the learned Subordinate Judge ought to have held that such a suit was not maintainable and on that view of the matter the learned Subordinate Judge was clearly wrong in holding that the plaintiffs had got a prima facie case for temporary injunction. The learned Advocate for the appellant has submitted that the prayer for declaration, as has been made in the suit, is a peculiar one and is not in keeping with the provision of law as incorporated in section 42 of the Specific Relief. The learned Advocate has argued that in view of the fact that the declaration does not relate to any legal character of the plaintiffs or any right to property as has been provided under. section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, the suit for such a declaration is clearly not maintainable and as such Liable to be dismissed and that the learned Subordinate Judge ought to have held that the plaintiffs had no prima facie case in support of their prayer for injunction. The learned Advocate has, in support of his contention, relied upon the decision of the Privy Council in the case of Sheoparsan Singh andothers Vs. Ramnandan Prashad Narayan Singh, L.R. 3 I.A. 91 same case, 20 C.W.N. 738. The suit in the said case was instituted by the plaintiffs against one Ramnandan Prashad and some others for a declaration that the plaintiffs were the nearest reversionary to one Bachu Singh who died allegedly leaving a widow, and as such plaintiffs were entitled to apply to the probate Court to get the probate of the Will issued to the Defendant Ramnandan revoked. Sir Lawrence Jenkins, in delivering the judgment' of the Privy Council, made the following observations after quoting the provision of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. 

 "A plaintiff coming under this section must therefore be entitled to a legal character or a right as to property. Can the plaints predicate this of themselves? Clearly not, and this is in effect, stated in the plaint, where they described themselves as entitled to Bachu Singh's estate in case of an intestacy after the death of the defendants widows. But as things stand, there is no intestacy: Bachu Singh's will has been affirmed in a Court exercising appropriate jurisdiction, and the propriety of that decision cannot, in the circumstances of this case, be impugned by a Court exercising any other jurisdiction." 

 The learned Advocate has also referred to the decision of the case of Snow White Food Product Co. Ltd. Vs. M/s. The Punjab Vanaspati Supply Co. in 49 C.W.N. page 172 in which an observation has been made by a Single Judge of the Calcutta High Court to the effect that section 42 of the Specific Relief Act is exhaustive and declaration outside the scope of the section cannot be granted. Reference has also been made by the learned Advocate to the case of Chowdhury Mohammad Manjural Haque and others Vs. Sebait Bissewar Banerjee 47 C.W.N 408 where a Division Bench of the Calcutta High Court has observed that the power of the Court to make a decree for such declaration is entirely governed by section 42 of the said Act, and that where the decree has effect of giving present relief as well, the power to make it will be governed by the general provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure, e.g. section 9 or Order 7, Rule 7 of the Code and not by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. Mr. Khondker has also cited before us a decision of the Division Bench of Madras High Court in the case of Krishnavani Ammal and another Vs. M. D. Soundaranarajaa and others, In A.I.R. 1945 Madras 53, in which it has been observed that there is no doubt: that section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. is not exhaustive, relying upon an earlier decision of the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council, namely Robert Fischer V s. Secretary of the State, in L.R. 26 I.A. 16, same case I.L.A. 22 Mad. 270, as well as two decisions of the Madras High Court namely, Ramchandra Rao Vs. Secretary of State; ILR 39 Mad. 808 same case A.I.R. 1916 Mad. 1061 and Secretary of State Vs. Sulbaras, I.L.R. 56 Mad. 749 same case A.I.R. 1933 Mad 618, but proceeded to add that there was no warrant for the proposition that a' suit for a declaratory decree would lie when a plaintiff was neither entitled to any legal character nor any right in the suit property. It is not .necessary for us to examine in this case the correctness of the principle that section 42 is not exhaustive and that there may be a suit for a declaratory decree outside the provision of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act as, in our opinion, in the instant case although not very expressive language has been used in the prayer portion in the plaint, the substance of the prayer is quite clear and it relates to a declaration as to plaintiffs right to the property in suit. In order to appreciate the real nature of the relief claimed by the plaintiffs we have quoted some portions of the plaint as well as the exact prayer made in the suit. The claim in substance sought to be made out in the plaint is that the plaintiffs have acquired a substantial share, i.e. -/8/- annas. and odd share in the suit property by right of inheritance from their father and that defendant No. 5 had no exclusive interest of her own in the disputed property and therefore defendant Nos. 1 and 2, by virtue of their purchase from defendant No. 5, or defendant No. 3, by virtue of his purchase from defendant Nos. 1 and 2 have not acquired any interest to the prejudice of the interest of the plaintiffs, which has devolved upon them by right of inheritance from their father. According to the allegations made in the plaint, the plaintiffs are in possession of the property in suit in exercise of their legal title and defendant No. 3 is not entitled to dispossess them during the pendency of the suit. The prayer, as has been made in the plaint, although not drafted, happily, I doubt in one's mind that what the plaintiffs were essentially seeking in the suit was a declaration that their right, title and interest have not been affected by the transaction of sale in favour of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 or in favour of defendant No. 3. We cannot therefore say that the suit as framed does not fall within the purview of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and that should be thrown out as not maintainable. We are unable to accept the contention of the learned Advocate for the appellants that the learned Subordinate Judge was wrong in holding that the plaintiffs have got a prima facie case for temporary injunction. 

 9. The other point which has been pressed by the learned Advocate for the appellant is that the suit really being one for a mere declaration that certain transactions of sale are void and not binding upon the plaintiffs, there is no scope for a temporary injunction in the matter and the learned Advocate in support of his contention has relied upon a decision in the case of Jit Lal Singh Vs. Ramleswari Prosad, in 16 Calcutta Law Journal page 535 in which Mukherjee J in delivering the judgment of the Bench has observed that an order for temporary injunction under Order 39 Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure can be sought only in aid of the prospective order for a perpetual injunction. If therefore, in the event of the plaintiff's success, he cannot obtain a decree for perpetual injunction, it is not competent for him to ask for a temporary injunction, during the pendency of the suit. In granting a temporary injunction the Court acts in aid of the legal right, so that the property may be preserved in status quo. The question as to the issue of temporary injunction was considered in that case under the provision of Order 39, rule 2 of the Code which specifically contemplated a suit for permanent injunction. A similar view was taken in a Division Bench decision of the Dacca High Court in the case of Kanti Ram Shil and another Vs. Sumitra Devi and others in 14 D.L.R. (Dacca) 272. But it has been pointed out in the case of Kazi Shamsuddin Ahmed Vs. Mst. Nuran Nehar in 21 D.L.R. (Dacca) page 41 that Supreme Court of Pakistan in the case of Sarbeswar Das Mohantli Vs. Baishnab Das Mohanta and others (C. A. No. 24-D of 1964) has laid down that a Court has jurisdiction to grant temporary injunction even in a suit for simple declaratory decree in an appropriate case. This view has also been adopted in a Division Bench decision of this Court in the case of Mrs. June Fergusen and others Vs. Ameenur Rasheed Chowdhury and others in 25 DLR (Dacca) page 1 same case 1972 Bangladesh Law Reports page 240. Having regard to the judicial,views which have been referred to above the jurisdiction of the Court to issue temporary injunction in a suit for a mere declaratory decree, can, in our opinion, no longer be doubted although such injunction may not be granted strictly under Order 39, rule 2 of the Code. We, therefore, do not find any substance in the contention of the learned Advocate on this point as well. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case we are of opinion that the order of temporary injunction which has been made by the learned Subordinate Judge has been properly made and the same cannot be interfered with in the appeal. The result is that this appeal fails and is dismissed with costs.
